title: Fantasy baseball streaming starting pitchers: Can you trust Quinn Mathews, Connor Prielipp?
description: Eric Samulski lists his favorite streaming starts of the week
fullText:
Welcome to your fantasy baseball starting pitcher happy place. This is a new column for me this year that will combine a few things I've done before. In this article, every Monday, you'll not only get a list of my favorite streaming starting pitchers for the week, but underneath that is also a breakdown of a few pitchers making interesting changes to their pitch mix. For this week, I'm not going to do unique pitcher analysis underneath this because I wrote an entire article on pitch mix and usage changes last week that you can check out here.

We should note that we are entering the final two weeks of the season, which means that we need to treat these schedules with a HUGE grain of salt. Teams are going to change around the schedule mid-week, so you're going to need to keep up on the news on Rotoworld during the week and also rely a little bit less on the Sunday streamers because they may lose those starts.

As far as which pitchers on this list you'll want to stream, your decisions will change based on your league type and settings. Since I'm listing starters for the whole week, I won't be able to provide a detailed analysis for each one; I'll highlight the matchup and offer some quick thoughts. As is usual with my articles, a streaming starter pitcher is rostered in less than 40% of Yahoo formats, so just keep that in mind as we're going through because I won't be mentioning pitchers who are rostered in more leagues than that. I also won't be mentioning pitchers that I would not start in any format.

Check out this week's MLB Power Rankings!

A Quinn Mathews two-step with your season on the line. Can you do it? I'm inclined to. I think both matchups are solid, and Mathews has been good enough over his last few starts. I think there's more strikeout upside than he showed, but there is some risk worry. Landen Roupp is super inconsistent, and it's hard to know if we can trust him, but the matchup is good. Sadly, Corbin Burnes just likely won't go deep enough into this game, which means you're hoping for four solid innings here. I would not trust Casey Mize, who has been struggling, to go on the road in Colorado.

Maybe people don't know that Griffin Jax looked good in his last start? I know his first start off the IL was a disaster, but he looked much better here and is a solid two-start pitcher for this week. I love this matchup at home. Andre Pallante is also in a good spot against a Giants team that is without Rafael Devers and is looking towards next season. Ryan Johnson is a much bigger risk, but I think you can get a quality start here, and Michael Soroka just hasn't been going deep enough into games, which worries me. Blade Tidwell is the ultimate risk, but I'm not opposed to you targeting the Cardinals offense.

I know Jared Jones is over the roster limit, but this is just in case you're thinking that you need to bench him against the Brewers. I do like the Merrill Kelly start against the Marlins, even though Kelly has been tough to trust lately. Same goes for Jake Bennett, who is clearly running on fumes right now, but gets a good matchup. We've been waiting for Cristian Javier to ride this new pitch mix to better results, and it might finally be happening. Erick Fedde has been pitching solid as a bulk reliever, which gives him a good chance at wins, and Yusei Kikuchi has actually been pretty good since coming off the injured list.

Not a lot of games on Thursday, so not a ton of options. I think Dustin May has been getting pretty unlucky of late, so I can trust him here against the Pirates. Anthony Kay is a bit tougher to trust, but the Tigers haven't been hitting the ball really well of late, so I can see rolling the dice.

Connor Prielipp is pitching better of late, but this is really about the matchup. The Angels are the worst team in the American League, and I think we can attack them with the majority of capable pitchers right now. I wish I knew what we'd get from Joey Cantillo, but he seems to be a conundrum every time out. I do love the matchup at home, though. Andrew Alvarez is risky, but he is pitching deeper into games, and I like the matchup here. I can't trust Luis Castillo, and Shane Drohan has not been pitching deep into games, which dampens a lot of his upside here.

I know Andrew Painter hasn't taken off like I expected because the fastball velocity and vertical movement have come and gone, but it was back in his last outing, and so I'll trust him here. I'll also trust Jacob Lopez because he's on the road; his last two home starts were not great. I listed Cal Quantrill and Bubba Chandler here to show you that I'm a bit more tepid on them this week, despite them both being over the roster limit. I'm also tepid on Jackson Jobe despite his one good game against the Rockies at home because, well, it was the Rockies outside of Coors. Hayden Wesneski gets a tough matchup, but the Braves offense has also been struggling of late. It's a roll of the dice, but I can see doing it.

Now we're coming in with a lot of the two-start weeks. All of Patrick Sandoval, Brandon Young, Davis Martin, Jonah Tong, and Cody Bradford are tough to trust because of their schedules, so I would rather avoid those two-start weeks. Landen Roupp has a good first start, so I can see taking the gamble there, and Dean Kremer has this really nice start against the Angels if you wanted to chance it against the Yankees to start the week. Griffin Jax finishes off his solid two-start week, as does Quinn Mathews, with Ryan Johnson being a gamble against a Minnesota offense that does hit for power if they ever decide to wake up.

title: Lampard 'gone by end of October' or 'nothing to worry about'? Fans on league start
description: Ian: The concerning thing is the impact of the tough fixtures on confidence, exacerbated by recruitment not focusing on players with any Premier League experience.  Terance: The Premier League is tough.  Look, the vast majority of football supporters like Frank Lampard, but, in my opinion, he should have recruited more players with Premier League experience, signed them on a two-year contract, and gone from there.
fullText:
We asked for your views on Coventry's difficult start to the season and whether Frank Lampard's team is being written off too soon.

Here are some of your comments:

Ian: The concerning thing is the impact of the tough fixtures on confidence, exacerbated by recruitment not focusing on players with any Premier League experience. While over a season the fixtures will even out, the harm done by playing the current top four in the league so soon cannot be underestimated.

Alan: If we weren't creating chances it would be a big problem, but we are so there is nothing to be worried about. When one comes the rest will follow

Terance: The Premier League is tough. Look, the vast majority of football supporters like Frank Lampard, but, in my opinion, he should have recruited more players with Premier League experience, signed them on a two-year contract, and gone from there. Why not Jamie Vardy? He knows where the goals are - maybe not a 90-minute player, but he scores goals (gone to Burnley now).

Andy: It's very simple - we have definitely improved the squad in the summer window, but we are still short of being a genuine Premier League team. We need at least one more striker and a midfield leader to have any slither of hope of staying in this league. Add to that, the players that got us into the top flight must up their game to the required level and very quickly.

Tony: Spent a lot of money on new players but only select three for a must win match - why? Expected better after much improved team performance against Manchester City. We need Tatsuhiro Sakamoto and Hadji Wright asap while the new players settle in. Team selections could be much better.

Harold: Sorry, but can't see Lamps turning this round. Book Xmas holidays now -gone by end of October at best.

Alan: Julian Laurens questions whether Frank Lampard is good enough to succeed with Coventry in the Premier League. IF he maintains his win percentage at 41%, we finish with at least 46 points - easily good enough!

title: Baltimore's offense looked terrific in the opener, but injuries at wide receiver are concerning
description: Lamar Jackson dropped back on third-and-16, and as the pocket collapsed, he somehow ducked between a couple of pass rushers before finding a running lane and taking off for the first down.  From the start, it was clear that the engine of Baltimore's offense was back.  Jackson threw for 324 yards and a touchdown and also ran for a score, looking as spry as Baltimore had hoped after an injury-plagued 2025.
fullText:
Lamar Jackson dropped back on third-and-16, and as the pocket collapsed, he somehow ducked between a couple of pass rushers before finding a running lane and taking off for the first down.

"Playing football," the two-time NFL MVP said. "Just playing football."

From the start, it was clear that the engine of Baltimore's offense was back. By the time the game was over, Jackson and the Ravens had amassed 506 total yards, making Jesse Minter a winner in his head coaching debut, 41-23 over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.

Jackson threw for 324 yards and a touchdown and also ran for a score, looking as spry as Baltimore had hoped after an injury-plagued 2025. The only real downers for the Ravens: a slew of offensive line penalties and two potentially problematic injuries to the receiving corps.

"I think the confidence grows when you prepare well," Minter said. "We put a lot of time over these last couple of weeks into this game plan, with it being the opener and the extra time that you have. So, you want to see the preparation pay off, and I felt like it really did in all three phases."

For a little while, Zay Flowers appeared headed toward an all-time great receiving day. He had a 49-yard catch-and-run on Baltimore's first offensive play that set the Ravens up at the 2. His 54-yard touchdown reception made the score 21-6. After five possessions, he had five catches for 150 yards — but his day was also done because of hamstring issues.

Rookie Ja'Kobi Lane had a touchdown catch wiped out by a penalty, and he ultimately left with a wrist injury.

The usual names produced in a big way. In addition to Jackson's work at quarterback, Derrick Henry ran for 144 yards and three touchdowns. Flowers was brilliant when he was in the game, and Mark Andrews had four catches.

The Ravens looked extremely well prepared on offense under new coordinator Declan Doyle.

"We have so many gifted players," Andrews said. "So many tools at his disposal, and he is using them. It is just so much fun, and we are going to continue to get better and focus and make big plays."

The Ravens committed 10 penalties for 86 yards, almost all on offense. A hold on new center Jovaughn Gwyn took a touchdown off the board. Rookie Vega Ioane, a first-round draft pick, was called for holding twice in the first half.

After a shaky preseason that led the Ravens to bring in some competition, Tyler Loop made field goals of 57 and 45 yards Sunday. The former was a career long.

"Obviously, you have to make kicks and things like that, and in the preseason, he had a couple of mishaps," Minter said. "But just the work ethic and the trust in the process in so many different things that he's been working on, I expected nothing less. I am really happy for him that he performed that way today."

Baltimore was solid defensively at times and forced two turnovers, but the Ravens allowed 102 yards rushing on 20 carries. Minter will surely see room for improvement.

Devontez Walker (groin) was inactive, and with Flowers and Lane injured the wide receiving group was pretty depleted by game's end. Practice squad elevation Chris Moore contributed on kick returns and with a 53-yard catch, but Baltimore could have issues if it is without Flowers next weekend.

This was the first time in franchise history the Ravens had a 300-yard passer, a 150-yard receiver and a 100-yard rusher in the same game.

Baltimore plays its home opener this weekend against New Orleans. The Saints lost 31-30 at Detroit in overtime in Week 1.

title: Kentucky Wildcats open as hefty road underdogs against Texas A&M

title: Palace frustrate Arsenal women as familiar problem returns
description: Arsenal had 30 shots and nine on target but were held 0-0 by Crystal Palace, leaving Renée Slegers with plenty to address before Manchester United.Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesArsenal’s first h...
fullText:
Arsenal's first home game ended in frustration with a 0-0 draw, as a former Arsenal goalkeeper thwarted attack after attack to keep a clean sheet. The statistics say it all: 30 shots, nine on target and no goals.

Renée Slegers made three changes to her starting XI, with Chloe Kelly, Kyra Cooney-Cross and Lotte Wubben-Moy coming in for Steph Catley, Kim Little and Olivia Smith.

The players who did not make the matchday squad were Géraldine Reuteler, Selina Cerci, Taylor Hinds and Isabella Damm. Daphne van Domselaar, Michelle Agyemang and Katie Reid all missed out due to injury.

The unused substitutes were Anneke Borbe, Catley, Smilla Holmberg and Elisa de Almeida.

Little, Smith, Stina Blackstenius, Caitlin Foord and Frida Maanum all came on as attacking substitutes as Arsenal tried to unlock the Palace defence.

In these kinds of attack-versus-defence games, once you score the first goal, you expect the floodgates to open. That did not happen. There were echoes of last season, when Arsenal lost the title to City by four points after drawing six matches despite losing only once.

It was interesting to see Slegers use Kelly on the left and Lisa Baum on the right, with both playing as inverted wingers, without really switching flanks during the game.

Also notable was how the full-backs worked with the wingers ahead of them.

Emily Fox and Baum, and Ona Batlle and Kelly, are combinations that still need work.

During pre-season, I found the Holmberg-Baum partnership very effective going forward and much more creative than Fox-Baum.

I also found the Georgia Stanway and Cooney-Cross double pivot interesting because both are deep-lying playmakers who want the ball, want to dictate the game and can play long passes to find space.

Playing together in a midfield three alongside Mariona Caldentey as the No 10 led to plenty of chances being created.

But could Arsenal have been more creative and efficient against a low block? I think a different midfield profile could help in those situations, as could a centre-back stepping forward to create overloads in certain areas of the pitch.

At the end of the day, the margins between success and failure are small, and they did not go Arsenal's way.

Finishing is the toughest job in football. Could the forwards all have done better in the final third, both with the final ball and their finishing? Definitely. I am sure that will be worked on in training.

Next weekend brings bottom-of-the-table Manchester United, who have conceded seven goals.

Arsenal will need to have their shooting boots on.

Right now, Manchester City are top of the league with six points. Five teams have four points: Chelsea, Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Crystal Palace, alongside Arsenal.

At the bottom of the table, Manchester United and Charlton Athletic have no points after two games, while Aston Villa, Birmingham City and Brighton & Hove Albion have one point.

Although Arsenal dropped two points, the damage could have been worse. They now need to make sure they take all three against Manchester United next Saturday.

title: Liverpool threaten to spoil Man United’s January plans for La Liga speedster
description: 2 Manchester United’s desire to sign Alejandro Balde is about to prove trickier given the latest developments from Spain.A left-back signing, a capable Luke Shaw back-up, was one the Red Devils were...
fullText:
Manchester United's desire to sign Alejandro Balde is about to prove trickier given the latest developments from Spain.

A left-back signing, a capable Luke Shaw back-up, was one the Red Devils were expected to make but did not last summer.

That failure has since come back to bite them. Three games in, United have already found themselves in a tricky position, with Shaw missing the last two games through injury.

United head coach Michael Carrick has ended up reverting Patrick Dorgu to left-back, and the Dane looks exposed in the position. United may need a better option there whenever Shaw is unavailable.

The winter transfer window might be a few months away, but if the chance arises to sign a left-back, INEOS would be wise to take it.

That said, who might the 20-time English champions go for? They are unlikely to pursue Lewis Hall, who has just committed his future to Newcastle United.

Landing Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert, their other top target, mid-season might also prove tricky.

United may therefore be wise to revisit their interest in Balde.

Had he pushed for a Barcelona exit, giving INEOS the motivation to pursue him, the two European giants could have agreed a deal to bring him to Manchester. Instead, the Spanish speedster opted to stay at Camp Nou and fight for his place.

So far, Hansi Flick has continued to overlook him, which has convinced many that, come winter, he will have had enough and opt to leave.

While United would have been the likely destination had he chosen to leave Barcelona, Sport now suggests Liverpool have joined as a serious suitor for the left-back.

The Spanish outlet reports:"[Balde] has been mentioned in connection with Liverpool. The Reds' Spanish manager, Andoni Iraola, would consider his signing interesting, especially if it represents a good transfer opportunity."

Liverpool's interest, if genuine, is not great news for United.

It could deny the Red Devils the free run they might otherwise have had at this transfer.

As a result, Barcelona may try to dictate terms over any potential deal. However, they cannot ask for much if the young full-back continues to warm the bench.

✅ Balde's long-term future at Barcelona is up in the air.

⚠️ No formal transfer talks are currently under way.

⚠️ Top-tier outlets are yet to confirm the claims.

This looks like classic media noise aimed at capitalising on Balde's situation at Camp Nou, a strategy designed to manufacture market interest and force long-term suitors, such as Man United, into making a move.

title: Why Team India player was penalised after Women's Asia Cup final
description: India pacer Kranti Gaud admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by Supriya Rani Das of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Match Referees. As a result, there was no need for a formal hearing.
fullText:
NEW DELHI: India pacer Kranti Gaud has been fined 10 per cent of her match fee for breaching the ICC Code of Conduct during the Women's Asia Cup final against Sri Lanka in Dubai on Sunday.

Gaud was found guilty of a Level 1 breach of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel.

Gaud breached Article 2.5 of the ICC Code of Conduct, which relates to "using language, actions or gestures which disparage, or which could provoke an aggressive reaction from a batter upon his/her dismissal during an International Match."

The incident took place in the first over of Sri Lanka's innings. After dismissing opener Imesha Dulani, Gaud gestured in the direction of the pavilion.

Gaud admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by Supriya Rani Das of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Match Referees. As a result, there was no need for a formal hearing.

On-field umpires Saleema Imtiaz and Shathira Jakir Jesy, third umpire Rokeya Sultana and fourth umpire Humaira Farah levelled the charge.

Along with the 10 per cent fine, one demerit point has been added to Gaud's disciplinary record.

It was her first offence in a 24-month period.

Level 1 breaches carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand and a maximum penalty of 50 per cent of a player's match fee. They can also result in one or two demerit points.

Pakistan have been fined five per cent of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate during their Women's Asia Cup semifinal against Sri Lanka on Friday.

G.S. Lakshmi of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Match Referees imposed the sanction after Pakistan were found to be one over short of the target after time allowances were taken into consideration.

Under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which deals with minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their team fails to bowl in the allotted time.

Pakistan captain Fatima Sana pleaded guilty to the offence and accepted the proposed sanction. Therefore, there was no need for a formal hearing.

On-field umpires Vrinda Rathi and Shathira Jakir Jesy, third umpire Rokeya Sultana and fourth umpire Rabab Ahsan levelled the charge.

title: Devine to leave Glentoran after two and a half years
description: Glentoran manager Declan Devine is set to leave the club amid the east Belfast outfit's poor start to the Irish Premiership season.
fullText:
Glentoran manager Declan Devine is set to leave the club amid the east Belfast outfit's poor start to the Irish Premiership season.

An agreement over his departure was reached on Monday with the Glens winless in their past three league games and sat eighth in the table with seven points from their opening six fixtures.

Devine's last game in charge was a frustrating 1-1 draw with Bangor at the Oval on Saturday and the full-time whistle was met by a chorus of boos from the home faithful.

Former Glens goalkeeper Devine took over at the 23-time league champions initially as interim boss in March 2024 after Warren Feeney was sacked.

He was given the role as permanent boss the following month and guided Glentoran to the County Antrim Shield in the 2024-25 season, their first trophy in five years.

But, despite significant investment in the playing squad, they have finished no higher than third under Devine and fell to defeat in back-to-back BetMcLean Cup finals against Cliftonville and Linfield in 2025 and 2026.

Glentoran now face Coleraine on Tuesday looking for a new manager for the fourth time since January 2023.

Glentoran owner Ali Pour warned on Saturday that the pressure was on Devine to deliver this season.

Pour explained that Devine had at his disposal a squad that he had "hand-picked" after being provided with "the biggest budget of any manager".

But, as has been the case for much of Pour's time at the club, big spending off the pitch has not returned success on it.

Pour was in attendance for Saturday's drab draw with Bangor when supporters certainly made their feelings clear.

Despite an inconsistent campaign last season, the Glens were in control of their own destiny in the title race with two games to go.

Knowing two wins would secure a first title since 2009, they drew 0-0 at home to eventual champions Larne before they were then thumped 6-2 by Coleraine on the final day, with the Bannsiders pipping them to second spot.

Disappointment from the previous season has perhaps seeped into the current campaign as they were knocked out of Europe at the first hurdle by RFS and then lost to rivals Linfield and suffered back-to-back defeats against Crusaders and Larne.

The loss of midfielder Cammy Palmer in the summer has been keenly felt, while injuries have hampered Devine in the early part of the new season too.

They have struggled for a focal point in the absence of last season's top scorer Pat Hoban, while new signing Conor McMenamin will need time to ensure his second stint at the Oval lives up to the expectation established by his brilliant first spell.

The Glens still have a talented squad for whomever comes in next, but they will have to change the mentality of the players, who Devine's assistant Tim McCann said on Saturday needed to start taking "accountability" for their "unacceptable displays".

With ground to make up already in the title race, Glentoran supporters will hope that the new boss can quickly spark a new manager bounce to inject some life into what has been a listless campaign.

title: It's same ol', same ol' with Cowboys defense as hype gets pushed aside by reality
description: The Giants had the ball three times in the second half.  New York was 9 of 10 on third down for the game before Jaxson Dart's kneel-down on third down on the final play.  Receivers ran free in the secondary, just as they did a year ago when the Cowboys gave up the most points with the fewest interceptions in franchise history.
fullText:
FRISCO, Texas (AP) — Same old Dallas defense.

Even with a new defensive coordinator — the youngest in franchise history in 34-year-old Christian Parker — and an overhaul of the roster, the Cowboys were just as bad as a year ago in a season-opening 28-20 loss to the New York Giants on Sunday night.

Maybe worse, if that's even possible.

The Giants had the ball three times in the second half. They had two eight-minute touchdown drives, then ran out the final 5:21 on the third possession. New York was 9 of 10 on third down for the game before Jaxson Dart's kneel-down on third down on the final play.

Receivers ran free in the secondary, just as they did a year ago when the Cowboys gave up the most points with the fewest interceptions in franchise history. The run defense was porous in key moments — just as it has been for years now.

There was so much hype about the arrival of Parker and first-round draft pick Caleb Downs. So much hype about the Cowboys sticking to the business of football in the offseason while avoiding the soap operas that often surround them.

Hype has been replaced by reality with the home opener set for Sunday against Washington in a matchup of NFC East rivals trying to avoid an 0-2 start in the division.

"Don't flinch," coach Brian Schottenheimer said when asked what he would say to Parker. "You're going to get humbled at times. It happens. He'll learn from it. We'll learn from it. He's going to be hardest on himself anyways, he and the defensive staff."

Schottenheimer went off on the young players, unleashing an expletive while trying to explain why Dallas simply didn't cover running backs in the flat, repeatedly.

"Those are going to happen, and we have to coach the young players better," Schottenheimer said. "But when you play young players, it's part of the deal, and they need to learn quickly."

While Dak Prescott led the offense to touchdowns the only two times the Cowboys had the ball after halftime, his interception on an attempted throwaway late in the first half was the most pivotal moment in the game. New York scored touchdowns on either side of halftime because of it, breaking a 7-7 tie.

One of the problems the defense posed a year ago was giving Prescott and company little margin for error. Prescott wasn't buying talk of a 2025 replay, though.

"No, they did a hell of a job on the other side," Prescott said. "I'm in this year, sorry."

The Cowboys mostly matched the Giants with third down efficiency. Dallas was 8 of 11. The first of the three failed conversions came on the first series, when George Pickens caught a slant for what appeared to be a first down before replay assist turned it into fourth-and-inches. Schottenheimer elected to punt, making it a three-and-out.

The Cowboys had one game last season when both CeeDee Lamb and Pickens failed to reach 50 yards receiving. It was the meaningless finale against the Giants when both played less than 50% of the snaps. Lamb did have a touchdown among his 44 yards on Sunday night. Pickens finished with 28 and had a huge drop on a deep throw four plays before Prescott's critical interception.

CB Cobie Durant, who led the NFL with three interceptions in the playoffs last season, is making a case to be a full-time player. He was in on 72% of the snaps and had the only pass breakup among defensive backs while also forcing a fumble.

RB Javonte Williams had little impact — until his taunting penalty on the last Dallas touchdown when he held the ball out toward an opponent as he crossed the goal line. Schottenheimer said he planned to go for the 2-point conversion to try to get Dallas within six. Instead, Brandon Aubrey missed the 48-yard PAT try.

Schottenheimer said safety Malik Hooker may have fractured a forearm, which would mean two starters and a key backup are already on injured reserve just a week into the season.

The Dallas defense entered Monday last in the NFL in Week 1 with an expected points allowed per play of 0.34. Even Carolina was better at 0.33, and the Panthers lost to Chicago 59-37. A year ago, one of the worst defenses in franchise history finished at 0.13 expected points allowed per play.

The Cowboys haven't opened with consecutive losses since 2010, when Wade Phillips was fired midseason with a 1-7 record as Dallas went on to finish 6-10.

title: No weekend game for Manchester derby VAR officials
description: The video assistant referee for the Manchester derby, Matt Donohue, and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, are not appointed for this weekend's Premier League games.
fullText:
The video assistant referee for the Manchester derby, Matt Donohue, and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, have not been appointed for this weekend's Premier League games.

The decision was made by the Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref's chief refereeing officer Howard Webb and the management team.

It follows Pro Ref admitting to an "error of judgement" in awarding Erling Haaland's winning goal for Manchester City at Manchester United on Sunday.

The striker scored in the 60th minute at Old Trafford when he turned in a shot at the back post from Josko Gvardiol's cross.

His effort was initially disallowed on the field for offside but, following VAR intervention, the goal was awarded as the Norwegian was ruled to have been played onside by Patrick Dorgu's boot.

However, there was debate as to whether the goal should have been disallowed for City midfielder Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, interfering with play as he dived attempting to head the ball in a central position before Haaland's finish.

"It was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective," said Pro Ref in a statement.

"However, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review."

City, who had Phil Foden sent off after 23 minutes, maintained their 100% league record from four games with the victory.

title: Wave place USWNT forward Catarina Macario on season-ending injury list
description: The San Diego Wave placed United States Women's National Team forward Catarina Macario on the season-ending injury list, the team announced Monday.
fullText:
Sept. 14 (UPI) -- The San Diego Wave placed United States Women's National Team forward Catarina Macario on the season-ending injury list due to a knee injury, the team announced Monday.

Macario, who joined the Wave in March from Chelsea, has yet to play in a game for the NWSL squad. She is signed through 2030.

"I'm obviously disappointed that I won't have the opportunity to represent the club on the field this season, especially with how much it means to me to be back home in San Diego," Macario said. "But the club and I have made a long-term commitment to each other and are focused on the big picture.

"My focus is on continuing my recovery so that when I do return, I can feel like myself again and give the team and our fans the best version of me."

Macario, 26, posted a photo of herself while on crutches Monday on Instagram. She said she underwent a minor procedure a few months ago and hoped to return this season, but opted to keep the "bigger picture in mind."

"We made a significant long-term commitment to Cat because we believe in her ability to make a lasting impact on this club," said Camille Ashton, the Wave's general manager and sporting director.

"While we are disappointed that she will not be available this season, we are focused on her health and on supporting her throughout this process."

Macario tore an ACL in 2022 while with French club OL Lyonnes. That kept her out of the 2023 World Cup. Additional knee issues kept her from the 2024 Olympics.

"To be completely honest, it sucks to find myself in this position again," Macario wrote on Instagram. "There's no way around how difficult it is to go through another rehab and spend more time away from the game I love.

"I miss football, I miss competing, and after coming home to San Diego, I wanted nothing more than to be out there with my teammates, representing this club and this city.

"But as difficult as that is to accept, I know what I'm working toward. More than anything, I want to get back to feeling fully like myself again: playing freely, without feeling limited, and giving the best of me for a long time to come.

"For now, that means being patient, trusting the work we're doing and continuing to build toward what's ahead."

The 2026 NWSL season will start Feb. 11. The Women's World Cup will launch June 24.

The Wave (13-8-3), who won three of their last four games, sit in fourth place in the NWSL standings. They will host the Kansas City Current at 10 p.m. EDT Friday in San Diego.

title: Ethan Davis injury update: Tennessee loses TE for season with ACL injury
description: Tennessee football coach Josh Heupel announced on Monday that Volunteers tight end Ethan Davis will miss the remainder of the season with an ACL injury.
fullText:
Tennessee football will be without one of its key offensive pieces for the rest of the season.

Volunteers coach Josh Heupel announced during his game-week news conference on Monday, Sept. 14 that senior tight end Ethan Davis will miss the remainder of the 2026 college football season with an ACL injury.

"Ethan Davis (with) an ACL injury will be gone for the remainder of the year," Heupel said.

He added: "I hate it for Ethan because of the work that he put in and his growth as a person and the player, and now his season is cut short. But the next guy has got to be prepared and take advantage of the opportunity."

Davis, a former All-SEC Freshman Team selection in 2024 and a preseason John Mackey Award watch list selection this season, will end his 2026 campaign with three receptions for 47 yards and two touchdowns. He had a 25-yard touchdown in Tennessee's Week 2 win at Georgia Tech.

As noted by Adam Sparks of the Knoxville News Sentinel, part of the USA TODAY Network, sophomore DaSaahn Brame and South Alabama transfer Trent Thomas are expected to see larger roles with Davis sidelined for the season.

The Vols moved to 2-0 on the season with their road win against the Yellow Jackets on Saturday, Sept. 12. Tennessee first-year quarterback Faizon Brandon completed 10-of-21 passes for 148 yards and two touchdowns, while DeSean Bishop ran for 147 yards and two touchdowns.

Tennessee hosts Kennesaw State on Saturday, Sept. 19 at 7:45 p.m. ET at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville.

title: San Diego Wave move Catarina Macario to season-ending injury list
description: The San Diego Wave FC have placed Catarina Macario on the season-ending injury list with what the club calls an "ongoing knee issue."
fullText:
The San Diego Wave FC have placed Catarina Macario on the season-ending injury list with what the club calls an "ongoing knee issue."

The move means that Macario's debut for the club won't happen until 2027, another frustrating development for the U.S. women's national team forward.

Macario signed with her hometown club in March, with the Wave paying a reported $300,000 fee to land the 26-year-old from Chelsea.

But Macario has yet to play for the Wave, as she's been listed as out with a "heel" injury on the NWSL's availability report since her arrival.

"I'm obviously disappointed that I won't have the opportunity to represent the club on the field this season, especially with how much it means to me to be back home in San Diego," Macario said in a club statement.

"But the club and I have made a long-term commitment to each other and are focused on the big picture. My focus is on continuing my recovery so that when I do return, I can feel like myself again and give the team and our fans the best version of me."

Macario has struggled with injury issues since tearing her ACL in 2022, a setback that forced her to miss the 2023 World Cup and would ultimately keep her out for nearly two years.

The Brazil-born forward has 29 caps for the USWNT, scoring 16 goals. She led the team in goals in 2025, scoring eight times in 10 games. But her latest injury will once again put her availability for a major tournament in doubt.

Macario will have to prove her fitness to USWNT coach Emma Hayes ahead of the 2027 World Cup, which kicks off in June in her home country of Brazil.

The forward has yet to play in a major tournament for the USWNT, having been forced to withdraw from the 2024 Olympic roster with knee issues after originally being named to the squad.

For the Wave, meanwhile, their playoff push will have to continue without the club's marquee addition this year.

"We made a significant long-term commitment to Cat because we believe in her ability to make a lasting impact on this club," said Wave general manager Camille Ashton. "While we are disappointed that she will not be available this season, we are focused on her health and on supporting her throughout this process."

title: The iPhone X Literally Changed How We Use Our Devices
description: Those touch gestures took some getting used to back in 2017.
fullText:
Welcome to a new series called Apple a Day, where sites in the CNET family are sharing pieces of Apple content from our archives—an article, review and/or video—daily from now through late September. In addition to Lifehacker, this series will include pieces from our sibling sites PCMag, Mashable, CNET, and Popular Science.

That was the year Apple released the iPhone X, introducing the device's most radical change since its first iteration. (Perhaps only to be surpassed this year by the iPhone Duo.) It's funny to think about it today, but back in 2017, the iPhone X's single pane of glass was disruptive, to say the least. Where was the Home button? Without it, how could you do anything? That confusion inspired Lifehacker to publish "The iPhone X Gestures You Should Master," a guide to navigating your newly designed iPhone.

We had to learn to swipe up from the bottom of the display to go home; to swipe along the bottom to switch from app to app; to swipe down from the top right to access Control Center; to swipe down from the top left to access Notification Center. We even had to relearn reachability: Instead of lightly double-tapping the Home button to bring the screen down, you had to swipe down on the bottom of the display.

Reviewing these things now, it all seems so obvious, even second nature. Nearly another decade has passed since we published that story, and by now, most iOS users are accostumed to a Home button-free life. But looking through the comments on this nearly decade-old piece, it's clear the transition was anything but smooth. One user complained about how smartphone gestures were making everything more confusing. Another bemoaned how switching between their iPhone and iPad meant jumping between two different gesture systems. Fast forward to 2026, and it's near impossible to imagine going back.

Apple didn't immediately stop making iPhones with Home buttons—it also released the iPhone 8 and 8 Plus the same year as the iPhone X—but the writing was on the wall. Soon after, only the SE line shipped with the old design, and even iPads adopted an edge-to-edge display.

With the launch of the iPhone 16e in 2025, Apple officially retired the once-essential Home button. Though you can still buy and use second-hand devices that have one (the 2022 iPhone SE can even run iOS 27), it's clear the company has moved on, and the gestures once so foreign they once prompted us to publish a guide to their use are now as innate as doing things the old way. Perhaps in another 10 years, wearables and hand gestures will have changed everything again, and we'll look back with nostalgia on an era when we had to touch our devices at all.

title: These Are the Best Countertop Appliances for Small Kitchens
description: They use less space and/or combine two or more traditional appliances into one.
fullText:
Even if you don’t cook all that much, you probably find yourself spending a lot of time in the kitchen. It’s where families gather, where coffee is made in the mornings, where meals are prepped. If you do cook a lot, you’re likely highly aware of how big or small your kitchen is. The average kitchen these days is about 160-170 square feet, but even that can feel tiny sometimes.

If your kitchen is smaller than that—or just feels too small—one way to open it up is to clear up counter space. If you’re looking to make your small kitchen feel even larger, check out these small and combo appliances that will make the most of your limited square footage.

Tiny kitchens are a logistical nightmare, whether you’re an accomplished cook who routinely produces restaurant-quality meals or someone who can—sometimes—cook a cromulent omelet. If someone on your list has to use math to calculate how to get the most out of their small kitchen, the Our Place Wonder Oven is your gift answer. This stylish, compact appliance has six functions in one, and replaces—at minimum—the toaster, air fryer, and convection oven. It can air fry, bake, roast, toast, broil, and reheat anything, and offers a steam infusion feature that makes everything come out perfectly moist. Everything else you might need—wire rack, air fry basket, bake pan, and crumb tray—are all included.

Your next stop is this nifty appliance that combines eight functions in one relatively compact unit. It’s a microwave, air fryer, convection oven, and broiler all in one. It’s large enough on the inside to cook a wide range of dishes, but it’s small enough to be stuffed into a cabinet if needed. If you need to leave it on the counter, it’s about 21 inches long, so it won’t eat up every available inch when you’re not actively using it.

If you don’t need the other functions, you can find smaller microwaves (like this one) that take up even less space. But even if you only use an air fryer once in a while, having that functionality combined with a microwave is a great deal.

Combining the functions of a blender, a food processor, and a mixer in one small unit, the Ninja Professional Plus Blender is ideal for folks who love to bake, make smoothies, and chop a lot of stuff. It’s less than eight inches deep and less than 10 inches wide, so it will unobtrusively tuck into just about any available space in your kitchen.

If you’re the only one drinking coffee in your house, you don’t need a bulky machine. This one-cup mini brewer from Keurig is ideal—it’s small, the pods make it super easy to use, and if you drink multiple cups, it brews quickly so you can just grab a refill as needed. Plus it’s less than five inches wide, so it will slide in anywhere.

If you’re not a fan of the pod coffee experience, this Hamilton Beach single-serve brewer is almost as narrow and lets you use your favorite grounds.

If you use a kettle, chances are it’s sitting on the stovetop right now. That’s fine as long as you’re not using your stovetop for other things—the moment you need to cook a meal, that kettle is just in the way. But this kettle will fold right into a drawer when you’re not using it.

Less than four inches wide, this little unit will toast two slices of anything without insisting upon itself. It’s got every feature you’ll find in a larger toaster, but its slim design means it can fit into spots that a normal toaster can’t. It could even be unplugged and slid into a drawer when not in use, if toast is an occasional thing in your home.

While a combination oven and air fryer makes the most sense from a space-saving point of view, if you air fry a lot, you might prefer to have a distinct unit. In that case, check out this model. Less than 10 inches wide and 12 inches deep, it’s a personal air fryer perfectly sized for one person and small jobs.

If you bake in a tiny kitchen, you know that stand mixers take over. The answer is kind of obvious: This compact hand mixer lets you tuck the beaters onto the side. That plus any large bowl will let you mix whatever you need without having to dedicate half your kitchen to a single appliance.

title: Manchester Storm call off game after 'technical issue with ice'
description: Manchester Storm call off their Challenge Cup match against the Nottingham Panthers at the AO Arena because of what the club call a 'technical issue with the ice'.
fullText:
Manchester Storm were forced to call off their Challenge Cup match against the Nottingham Panthers because of what the club called a "technical issue with the ice" at the AO Arena.

The Storm's first competitive fixture at the city centre venue in 24 years was scheduled to start at 16:00 BST on Sunday.

But supporters were faced with a lengthy wait before the club announced on social media that the match was suspended - just minutes before a revised 19:30 start.

"Unfortunately today's Manchester Storm game has been suspended due to a technical issue with the ice," the Storm said in the statement.

"We sincerely apologise to supporters and ticket holders for the disruption and would like to thank everyone in attendance for their patience."

Fans have been advised to retain their tickets, which will be valid for the rescheduled fixture on 14 October.

The venue, at the heart of Manchester, had staged a concert by American actor and singer Hilary Duff on Saturday evening - less than 24 hours before the ice hockey match.

Having left Planet Ice in Altrincham, the Storm returned to AO Arena on 6 September with a sold out pre-season friendly against the Sheffield Steelers.

Founded in 1995, the team played in the then newly opened Manchester Arena as a tenant and became inaugural champions of the Ice Hockey Superleague in 1996.

They left the arena in 2002 but said they have returned to take advantage of a growth in ice hockey's popularity to get more fans to the 23,000-capacity venue.

title: From Challenger Tour to Davis Cup - GB's Samuel on 'surreal' year
description: Briton Toby Samuel is to make his Davis Cup debut for Great Britain after what he calls a "surreal" 12 months.
fullText:
Toby Samuel says it was "one of the best moments in my life" when he was selected in Great Britain's Davis Cup team to face Ecuador this weekend after a breakthrough year.

The 23-year-old was handed his maiden Davis Cup call-up after a rapid rise over the past 12 months, climbing into the top 100 in the world rankings and making his debut in three Grand Slams.

"It's surreal being in this position now from where I was eight, nine months ago, [when I was] hopefully trying to play some Challengers, and now I'm sat here ready to play the Davis Cup - it's crazy," he told BBC Points West.

Samuel joins Arthur Fery, Cameron Norrie, Henry Patten and Lloyd Glasspool in the squad to face Ecuador at London's Copper Box arena.

Samuel breaks more new ground with first win at a Slam

Fery named in GB Davis Cup team to face Ecuador

Samuel, who is from Winchester and trains in Bath, was in New York having just made his US Open debut when he was told the news.

"I was out in New York walking around when I got a call up from Leon [Smith] the captain saying, 'congratulations, you've been selected,'" Samuel added.

"It was unbelievable, it was one of the best moments of my tennis life, to get called up to that, it's what every British player wants, to represent their country and play for their country."

At the US Open, Samuel claimed his first victory in a Grand Slam with a dominant win over Tomas Machac before losing to 18th seed Jiri Lehecka in the next round.

It has been a year of firsts as Samuel also reached the main draw of the French Open, coming through three rounds of qualifying before losing to world number eight Alex de Minaur in the first round proper.

Weeks later, he was handed a wildcard entry at Wimbledon and took Czech 15th seed and French Open semi-finalist Jakub Mensik to five sets.

"At first it was a completely new experience, I was pretty nervous going to those tournaments, seeing the top guys there in the locker rooms and playing against them - I was sort of shaking a little bit on court," Samuel said.

"But after the second or third time I did it I got more used to it and I felt like I was a lot calmer on the court, which helped me to go deep."

Stepping up to the top-tier tournaments has meant mentally and physically there has been a lot for Samuel to learn this past year.

With Challenger Tour matches played over three sets, this is the first time Samuel has consistently played five-set matches.

Being able to play for three, four or even five hours is a "new thing", although he feels his serve and forehand have improved significantly.

"Before they were good but they weren't really scaring people," he said. "Now they're my biggest weapons and I can take matches with them."

title: Women's rugby not to blame for region axe - WRU
description: The director of women's rugby at the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has hit back at "embarrassing" claims over why a men's region is being axed.
fullText:
The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has hit back at claims the women's programme is a financial drain on the men's game.

WRU women's rugby director Nadine Griffiths said allegations she had read on social media that a region is to be cut because of investment in the women's game were "embarrassing".

And she added the women's game had in fact made money for the governing body.

The Union has had a professional women's programme since the start of 2022 and there are now more than 40 contracted players.

But plans to axe one of the four men's professional regions - most likely Scarlets or Ospreys - has stirred hostility.

"I'm really disappointed and slightly embarrassed by some of the comments I read online about the women's game taking money from the men's game," she said.

"It doesn't. There are five different budget lines, including the men, women, [Principality] stadium and community game."

Griffiths appointed WRU director of women’s rugby

WRU keen for two Welsh sides to join PWR

Griffiths added the women's game generated £1.7m last year and, compared with the men's side of the sport, has more potential for commercial growth.

"If we look at the men's game we are hitting ceilings in terms of where our commercial growth opportunities are, there's only so much more we can charge for tickets, there's only so many people we can get into the ground," Griffiths said.

"Our women's game is a growth area and provides us an opportunity to really bring in some serious cash into Welsh rugby as a whole.

"It's bringing people who don't traditionally watch rugby and again it leads into that commercial growth where we're selling more jerseys and watching more games. So it actually lends into growing Welsh rugby as a whole."

Griffiths has been in post since June and is part of the WRU's executive team.

Her current priority for the women's game is visibility - building the profile of not only the senior team, but also pathways and grassroots rugby.

She accepts that is not helped by the miserable current form of the the senior side who are without a win in their last nine Test matches and have slumped to an all time low of 13th in the world.

"We can't hide from the fact that results matter," said the former international.

"The litmus test will be the WXV competition. It gives us a brilliant opportunity to test our progress playing against three sides that are ranked higher than us."

Wales open their campaign against South Africa on Friday at Cardiff Arms Park (19:15 BST) and play USA at the same venue eight days later. They then travel to Japan for two Tests in October.

"[Results] are not going to come overnight, we're building a house and we have to build those foundations," Griffiths said, pointing to encouraging results from the under-18s and under-21s sides.

Head coach Sean Lynn also selected eight uncapped players in his WXV squad.

"It shows us that our pathways are working. When they are working and you've built that competition for places, eventually results will come."

title: Familiar questions for Man Utd, now Carrick must find answers
description: After one win in four Premier League games, the problems are mounting for Manchester United and manager Michael Carrick.
fullText:
For the third time in less than 10 months, Manchester United have been beaten by opponents reduced to 10 men before half-time.

While the arguments raging around the 1-0 home defeat by Manchester City have centred around the official apology from Pro Ref to United for what they say was "an error of judgement" around Erling Haaland's matchwinner, the inquest will go much deeper at the club's Carrington training ground.

After pushing back on the idea four points from three games wasn't a great start at Everton last weekend, head coach Michael Carrick now accepts "there is no getting away" from the fact four points from four games is below expectations.

One win, at home to newly-promoted Ipswich, means so many questions - around recruitment, team selection, substitutions, tactics and Carrick himself - will now start to be asked ahead of a huge week.

"We don't need a break or a restart," said Carrick. "We've just got to move on and get winning again."

United entertain Brighton in the Carabao Cup on 16 September, before a trip to Fulham four days later.

If nothing else, Carrick needs his side to deliver to prevent a new three-week international break being filled with external inquests around what is going wrong at Old Trafford.

Speaking in his press conference after the game, new City boss Enzo Maresca accepted Phil Foden's red card made the game more difficult for his side.

However, he also highlighted why he knew it would also be a problem for United.

"They are a team that loves transitions and space in behind," he said.

"With 10 players, we just dropped and waited for them, so we didn't concede any transitions and didn't concede any space in behind. That is why the game became more difficult for us and for them."

United have been more effective as a counter-attacking team since Jose Mourinho arrived at the club over a decade ago. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer wanted to change it, but never quite got there.

The same, to an extent, is true of Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, both of whom came to United after achieving success in a domestic league where their side dominated the opposition. As a player, Carrick liked to get on the ball and not give it away. It is fair to assume that is what he wants from his players.

Keeping the ball is one thing. Having the vision and skill to keep possession and create chances against opponents quite prepared to sit in, deny space and keep their shape is another.

United's summer recruitment strategy was based around their midfield. Yet, with Youri Tielemans yet to find top form, Carlos Baleba still to make his debut and Andrey Santos dropped to the bench after the opening game at Hull and not used at all against City, the overall impact of their £155m summer spend has been limited.

At the same time, with Luke Shaw's 41-game run of consecutive Premier League starts coming to an end, there was no fresh back-up at left-back, as most observers expected.

And the introduction of Netherlands forward Joshua Zirkzee – someone who had been available for transfer all summer – for Marcus Rashford seven minutes from time as one of only two United substitutes, gave a strong indication the overall depth in Carrick's squad is not at the level required.

Bruno Fernandes won the PFA and Football Writers' Player of the Year awards last season for an outstanding campaign when he scored nine goals and claimed a Premier League record 22 assists.

So far this season, he has scored three times and has one assist. The goals record is good, but the assists are not. More importantly, his overall impact seems to have dipped.

Some observers felt he looked tired against City, which only heightened questions around his involvement against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK in the Champions League.

Despite their lowly ranking, it was understandable why Carrick would take no chances with his team selection as United returned to Europe's elite competition after a two-year absence.

However, with his side three goals up at the break and knowing there was a three-day turnaround to the City game, it was puzzling why Carrick elected to leave his skipper on the pitch for the full 90 minutes as he chose to use all five substitutes.

Now into the final year of his contract, which United have the option to extend to the summer of 2028, a continued over-reliance on Fernandes is a concern.

Carrick was appointed head coach on a permanent basis with a two-year contract in May after presiding over 12 victories in 17 games when in temporary charge following Amorim's dismissal.

While most said Carrick deserved his shot at the job full-time, others said it smacked of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's appointment, also after impressing in interim charge in 2019.

Solskjaer's record is decent and he remains the only United boss from the post Sir Alex Ferguson era to deliver successive top three finishes.

Yet the Norwegian never shrugged off claims he was not an elite coach. Critics will continue to argue the same is true of Carrick until he proves them otherwise.

When City were reduced to 10 men, did he go for the jugular?

"I thought we had a fair bit of the initiative, especially second half," he said. "Before they scored, I thought we were better.

"I thought we could improve on the second half of the first half. I thought we'd come out at half-time and build momentum. We hit the post, and the game was building the way we wanted. Then the goal obviously had a big impact.

"We could have finished the game better. We could have been a little bit more creative."

No-one is panicking just yet, but United's start to the season has raised familiar questions. Carrick needs to find the answers.

title: Maldini driving licence suspended after car crash
description: Italy international Daniel Maldini has his driving licence suspended following a car crash in Milan.
fullText:
Italy international Daniel Maldini has had his driving licence suspended after he was found to be over the legal alcohol limit following a car crash in Milan.

Maldini, son of Italy and AC Milan legend Paolo and grandson of the similarly feted Cesare, was one among six people to suffer minor injuries after his Porsche Carrera 4 collided with another vehicle in the early hours of Sunday.

The attacking midfielder had scored the winning goal for Cagliari in a 2-1 win against his parent club Atalanta in Serie A just hours before the accident.

Milan city police confirmed to BBC Sport that there had been a road traffic accident involving the 24-year-old footballer.

It said: "Mr Maldini was administered a breathalyser test at the scene" and his "driving license was confiscated following a positive result".

He was taken to hospital for precautionary checks before being released.

According to reports, an initial breath test carried out by the police at the scene of the accident recorded a blood alcohol level of 0.91 grams per litre, while a second reading registered 0.89 g/l - both higher than Italy's legal limit of 0.5 g/l.

In a statement, Cagliari said Maldini had "undergone toxicological screening following recent media reports" and that "all tests returned negative results".

The club added Maldini will join the squad for training on Monday to prepare for the team's forthcoming fixtures.

Maldini became became the third generation of his family to play for Italy when he made his debut against Israel in a Nations League fixture in 2024.

He has made six appearances for his country, with the latest coming in September 2025.

title: Somerset and Notts chase history, Bears also in hunt
description: Somerset, Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire are separated by just five points with two matches of the 2026 County Championship to go.
fullText:
With two games left of cricket's County Championship, three teams are separated by only five points vying to be the champion team of 2026.

Somerset, Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire enter the final straight all with realistic hopes of holding the trophy on Sunday, 27 September.

None of the sides play each other, so attention will have to be spread across six matches in the final two rounds to see who comes out on top when the music stops.

Throw in bonus points, and those imponderables of possible rain and bad light - and even the toss of a coin - and it's impossible to work out quite where this title race is going to go.

Somerset could be champions this week if they win and Notts and Warwickshire both lose, yet they could be third by Friday night and outsiders. It really is that close.

Let's start with the current leaders and the most romantic tale of all - Somerset. One of only three counties never to have been crowned champions, this is the holy grail.

Think of Boston Red Sox's 'Curse of the Bambino' 86-year wait between World Series titles, Hibernian's 114-year yearning to win the Scottish Cup again, Mayo's success in the All-Ireland Gaelic Football in July after 11 successive defeats in the final. Somerset's quest for the County Championship is of a similar ilk.

They had that great team in the late 1970s and early 1980s of Ian Botham, Joel Garner and Viv Richards which amassed plenty of one-day glory, while in recent years, there has been T20 Blast success.

But the Championship - the standard bearer for the county game - has remained elusive, and in a cricket-mad town like Taunton, excitement is building once again.

Of course, they have been close before. Between 2001 and 2019, they finished runners-up on no fewer than six occasions in the title race.

Tom Abell, Lewis Gregory, Craig Overton and Jack Leach were all part of that last side to come second and they remain integral members of the team now.

Overton has had an outstanding season with ball and bat, but he is wise enough to know the pitfalls of looking too far ahead.

"There's still a long way to go in this Championship and so much cricket to be played," he told BBC Radio Somerset.

"We've just got to keep doing our thing, keep doing the basics and see where we are at the end of this game."

Nottinghamshire were the underdogs 12 months ago as they prevented Surrey from winning four titles in a row, including a memorable victory at The Kia Oval.

This season, they have been the side to beat as they try to become the first Notts side to retain the title.

Joe Clarke has been the stand-out batter on the county circuit with a whopping 1,240 runs, almost 300 more than anyone else in Division One, while the bowling attack led by Olly Stone and Dillon Pennington has caused problems for all batting sides.

However, a failure to beat struggling Leicestershire earlier this month allowed Somerset to nip ahead of them and a tense 54-run success over Hampshire kept the margin between the top two at four points.

"We all knew coming into this week what was needed to really keep us amongst it heading into the two final games," said Stone, who took 9-95 in the Hampshire win at Trent Bridge.

"We go to Sussex now and they're playing good cricket at the moment and then we come back home against Yorkshire when we'll know what we have to do.

"Hopefully we can push hard to bring it home again."

With so few points separating the top three, it's worth reminding everyone how points are earned in the County Championship.

There are a maximum of 48 points available in the final two matches, but Somerset could win the last two games and still not finish top, given the variations in bonus points.

Fans will be out with their calculators during the four days as they work out the permutations for the teams involved.

Batting bonus points (for runs scored in first 110 overs of first innings):

Bowling bonus points (for wickets taken in first 110 overs of first innings):

Therefore a team can accrue up to eight bonus points to go with the points for winning, drawing and losing, with the possibility of a full 24 points on offer for a win.

While Somerset and Nottinghamshire chase historical, landmark successes, Warwickshire have no such burden.

If the other two are Roger Federer and Rafa Nadal, the Bears are the Novak Djokovic, coming up quietly on the rails to potentially spoil the party.

Ex-England bowler Chris Woakes led them to a thrilling one-wicket triumph over Sussex last month and they have dominated their past two matches, winning both by an innings as they go in search of a ninth Championship and first since the three-conference Covid season of 2021.

The Edgbaston side needed little more than 150 overs to take those 40 wickets, with their seam attack, led by Ethan Bamber, firing on all cylinders, a fact acknowledged by captain Ed Barnard.

"It was nice to get some rewards, I think I've bowled well all year and we've got a great attack with a great spinner, we're in a fortunate place at the moment," he said.

"It feels really exciting. We're trying not to think about it too much and obviously there are two massive games to go."

With so much at stake, the BBC will be right across the remaining two rounds of the County Championship.

title: Arsenal to contact Pro Ref over Konsa penalty
description: Arsenal will contact refereeing body Pro Ref over the incident that saw Ezri Konsa concede a penalty in Saturday's win over Sunderland.
fullText:
Arsenal will contact refereeing body Pro Ref over the incident in which Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty in Saturday's win over Sunderland.

Konsa and Black Cats defender Dan Ballard were involved in a physical exchange inside the penalty area in which the Arsenal defender was adjudged to have fouled the Sunderland player for excessive holding.

After the game Gunners manager Mikel Arteta criticised the decision, and it is understood the Premier League champions will hold talks with the professional referee's body for an explanation as to why the penalty was awarded.

It is understood Arsenal are keen to avoid major refereeing decisions impacting on results and want clarity over how referee John Brooks came to his decision.

Brooks initially awarded Sunderland the spot-kick on the field, and the decision was backed up by the video assistant referee (VAR).

"The referee's call of penalty to Sunderland for a holding offence by Konsa on Ballard was checked and confirmed by VAR," read a statement published by the Premier League Match Centre.

But after the game Arteta said: "This is not acceptable at this level.

"I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they think to give a penalty in that situation, or the way the VAR has to intervene.

"So I don't know what to think. I'm sad that we have to discuss this after such a beautiful game, that at this level has the gravity of that. Because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship.

"At this level, with all the work we put in, this cannot happen."

Match of the Day pundits Ashley Williams and Thomas Frank both said Sunderland should not have been awarded a penalty, claiming that Arsenal should have had a free-kick.

"I think he's got it completely wrong," said Williams. "It's almost like a perfect hip toss in judo [from Ballard]. In no way is it a penalty."

title: McCullum wants Pietersen to challenge methods
description: Former batter Kevin Pietersen accused England players of not trying on last year's tour of India.
fullText:
England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum says he wants newly appointed mentor Kevin Pietersen to challenge his methods.

Pietersen criticised England players during the tour of India last year, saying none could say they "did everything they can to try and help England win".

Former batter Pietersen has joined the limited-overs set-up as a specialist mentor until next autumn's 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

"That [Pietersen's comments] was one of the first things we talked about," McCullum told BBC Sport.

"He said 'gee, I was just criticising you not long ago'.

"I said I don't care about that. Some of it's fair and some of it would need some explanation, but I have no problem with that.

"It's healthy when you create an environment where you're able to challenge.

"That's one thing I want him to do. It's not just bury himself in the batting per se, but look across the entire environment, look across how we run things and what we do, and if there's anything you pick up then just come and challenge me on it.

"Him and I get on well. We had natural respect playing against each other and we spent a bit of time together in the last little while, and I'm super excited to have him as part of our support staff as well."

Pietersen joined up with the squad on Sunday before the first of three T20s and three ODIs against Sri Lanka in Southampton on Tuesday.

Tuesday, 15 September at 18:30 BST

McCullum said Pietersen was "shocked" when he first called him about "helping us challenge for a World Cup".

The pair had conversations to reach an agreement and McCullum said Pietersen was "unbelievably enthusiastic" about the prospect.

"The energy he's brought to the group already has been immense and you know I feel very privileged for us to be able to have him as a resource within our dressing room," said McCullum.

"He was obviously a brilliant cricketer. He viewed the game quite differently. He was a winner and he was a guy who left no stone unturned when it came to his preparation.

"A lot of these guys grew up watching Kev play and idolised him.

"As a coach, you're trying to provide these guys with the best environment so that they can try and achieve what they want. Adding Kev is certainly that."

England will hand a debut to Derbyshire opener Aneurin Donald in the first T20, with Phil Salt missing through injury.

Donald, who was born in Wales, has impressed in the T20 Blast and The Hundred with Trent Rockets this year and has the highest strike-rate - 232 - of any batter to have faced at least 50 balls in T20s this year.

Pace bowler Jofra Archer is rested after playing all three Tests against Pakistan, but Josh Tongue is included.

England team to face Sri Lanka in first T20: Aneurin Donald, Jos Buttler, Harry Brook (capt), Tom Banton, Jordan Cox, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Liam Dawson, Josh Tongue, Sonny Baker, Adil Rashid.

McCullum's sole responsibility is now for the white-ball side after he was sacked as Test coach following the series defeat by New Zealand in June.

England have appointed fellow New Zealander Stephen Fleming to the role.

The pair must juggle the workloads of England's players as they bid to regain the Ashes from Australia next summer before the World Cup.

"We've already been chatting around how we're going to try and manage some of the workloads of players and make sure we still get our best players available for the big series," said McCullum.

"We'll sit down in the coming days and map out a bit of a pathway for a few guys, but naturally guys can't play all year round.

"You're going to have to work out times that you can take them out of the physical duties of international cricket, freshen up, and then other times that you have them all ready to go.

"They will be easy conversations between two good mates with the motivation of what's right for English cricket."

The end of McCullum's reign as Test coach was tainted by off-field issues in Australia during the Ashes, while captain Ben Stokes and seamer Gus Atkinson missed the second Test against New Zealand in June after an incident in a London nightclub.

Since McCullum's departure seamer Brydon Carse has been involved in a nightclub incident while celebrating a victory for Durham.

Test captain Joe Root said he was "hacked off" and had had a "very strong discussion" in the changing room.

McCullum said he is in "total agreement" with Root and that he wants his white-ball side to be the "fittest, strongest, most dynamic, most robust cricket team in the world".

"There is a lot of talent which sits within English cricket and if people aren't prepared to make those sacrifices and to commit to what you're trying to achieve on the field, then other guys will be given those opportunities," said McCullum.

"It's important for Carsey now to just get his house in order and then work his way back towards banging down the door to play for England, because he's still got a long runway in front of him in terms of his career."

title: Is the Premier League already a two-team title race?
description: Four games is far too soon to be talking about who is in or out of the title race... isn't it? BBC Sport asks if this is already a two-horse race.
fullText:
Four games is far too soon to be talking about who is in or out of the title race... isn't it?

And yet Arsenal and Manchester City, who have been the top two in three of the past four seasons, look a level above everyone else so far.

Is it already a two-horse race?

With new (or newish) managers, Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham were all looking for better things this season.

But so far their starts range from shaky to shambolic.

How Premier League table looks after four games

Arsenal and Manchester City are the only two teams with 12 points from four games.

They are already four points above third-placed Hull City - who despite their brilliant early form may not consider themselves in any kind of title equation - and five above the rest.

Arsenal are the defending champions and pre-season title favourites.

Under manager Mikel Arteta they ended a 22-year title drought last season with what was often perceived to be an attritional style of play.

They started this season with a hugely impressive 3-0 victory over Manchester City in the Community Shield.

And they have carried on with victories over Coventry, Aston Villa, Chelsea and Sunderland - plus Napoli in the Champions League.

Including last season, they are now on a nine-game winning run in the league - and last lost in any competition in 90 minutes to City on 19 April.

Unlike Arsenal, City do not have the continuity this season with boss Pep Guardiola leaving after six titles, including a Treble, in 10 years.

Enzo Maresca, once his assistant, has taken over and led them to four wins from four in the league after that loss in Cardiff to the Gunners.

They have beaten Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Coventry - plus Porto in the Champions League - before their controversial 1-0 success at Manchester United on Sunday.

Erling Haaland scored the only goal, with the Premier League's refereeing body later admitting a mistake as it should have been ruled out for offside.

Despite their 100% starts, the underlying numbers behind Arsenal and City's starts do not imply total dominance.

Brighton (13) and Chelsea (10) have scored more goals than the eight that the top two have both netted.

For shots, Arsenal and City rank 10th and 11th and touches in the opposition box they are sixth and fifth respectively.

Arsenal have only conceded once and City have let in two goals - two of the best records in the league.

Refereeing body admits judgement error over Haaland derby winner

Intelligence & resilience key in statement win for Maresca's Man City - Murphy

'Today the game was unprotected' - Arteta fumes but Arsenal survive

The next three favourites to win the title with most bookmakers - in order - were Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United - with Tottenham some way back.

Chelsea and Liverpool both sacked their managers, bringing in Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola respectively in the summer.

United and Spurs both changed manager earlier in 2026, with Michael Carrick and Roberto de Zerbi having their first pre-seasons.

Last season, Chelsea finished 10th, Liverpool as defending champions were fifth, and Spurs came 17th - with United ending up third after turning things around under Carrick.

So for all four hopes were high this was going to be a better season.

Chelsea are fifth, with only one defeat so far, and have scored 10 goals... but conceded nine - the fourth worst record in the division.

They have conceded two or more goals in each of their first four matches of a Premier League season for the first time since 2015-16.

Liverpool are down in seventh, unbeaten after four games - but three of those are draws.

It is just the third time in the last 63 seasons they have failed to win either of their first two home league games.

United are 13th with four points - equalling their worst start to a Premier League season since 1992-93... level with last season.

They have had more shots than anybody else in the league - 84 - and the second fewest shots conceded (41).

Despite that they have conceded as many as they have scored - seven.

Spurs would not have considered themselves in the title race after two 17th-placed finishes but would have hoped for a better start as they currently sit... 17th.

And even worse than that, it was the first time in the club's history they have failed to score in their first four league games.

Toothless Spurs blank again as new era turns into a false dawn

More dropped points at Anfield - is it too early for Liverpool to worry?

New system, same problems - Alonso not happy with 'soft' Chelsea

Prior to this campaign, 80 teams in the English top-flight have won their first four league games of the season.

Of those, just 24 went on to win the title, proving that early dominance does not necessarily mean a side will last the pace.

In the Premier League era, nine of the 28 sides to win four on the bounce at the start of a season have gone on to lift the title, most recently Manchester City in 2023-24.

As the graphic below shows, there have been just six previous Premier League seasons in which two or more teams have won each of their first four fixtures.

And the bad news for the chasing pack is that just two clubs have won the Premier League having been five or more points behind after four games.

Manchester United did it five times under Sir Alex Ferguson (1992-93, 1996-97, 1998-99, 2007-08 and 2008-09), while Pep Guardiola's Manchester City acheived the feat in 2020-21.
